subject.title: Feature: Webchat / Control UI inline button support (buttons parameter, callback RPC, capabilities config)

question: Should WebChat inline interactions use the shared typed presentation action contract plus an authenticated chat.callback Gateway RPC, and should v1 add any WebChat capability/config key?
rationale: The feature gap is clear, but the first implementation would commit OpenClaw to a public WebChat protocol, callback authorization model, and possibly a new config surface.

options.title: Adopt typed presentation RPC v1
options.body: Use final-only typed presentation/action blocks, add authenticated chat.callback, implement Control UI rendering, and leave webhook routing out of the first version.

options.title: Split protocol before UI
options.body: Approve the Gateway protocol and authorization contract first, then add Control UI rendering and click-state behavior in a follow-up PR.

options.title: Support legacy buttons compatibility
options.body: Accept a broader dual-contract surface that maps legacy buttons alongside presentation, with explicit migration and compatibility tests.

recommendation.title: Adopt typed presentation RPC v1
recommendation.body: Use final-only typed presentation/action blocks, add authenticated chat.callback, implement Control UI rendering, and leave webhook routing out of the first version.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal on the typed presentation contract and broad Gateway/chat direction involved in this decision.
